blocks.instruction: Read each situation carefully and answer the questions.

items.label: (a)
items.q: Look at a ₹ 10, ₹ 20 or ₹ 50 note at home. Write two things you see printed on it.
items.answer: Any two (1 each): the value of the note; the name Reserve Bank of India; the picture of Mahatma Gandhi; the national emblem (Ashoka lions); many Indian languages on the language panel; a picture on the back (e.g. Konark Sun Temple on ₹ 10, Ellora caves on ₹ 20, Hampi chariot on ₹ 50).

items.label: (b)
items.q: Navya wants to post a letter to her cousin. Write the journey of the letter from the postbox to her cousin's house.
items.answer: The letter is dropped in the postbox; the postman collects it and takes it to the post office (1). The post office sorts letters by region and sends them to their destination, where a postman delivers it to the cousin's house (1).

items.label: (c)
items.q: Navya saw a metro train and a flyover from the bus. How do these two help travellers?
items.answer: Metro trains travel very fast and carry many people (1). Flyovers are high roads that let vehicles move above busy roads and crossings, saving time (1).

answerPoints.point: Flyover – above busy roads, saves time

items.label: (d)
items.q: Stand facing the rising sun in the morning. Which direction is in front of you, and which direction is behind you?

items.label: (e)
items.q: Dada ji showed Navya his bank passbook. Write two important things printed on the first page of a passbook.
items.answer: Any two (1 each): customer's name; account number; IFSC code; bank and branch name; address; opening date; mobile number.

blocks.instruction: Answer the following questions in two or three sentences.

items.label: (i)
items.q: Write the full form of ATM. Write two ways in which it helps people.
items.answer: Automated Teller Machine (1). It lets us take out money any time we need it (1), so we do not have to visit the bank and wait in long queues (1).

answerPoints.point: No need to queue at the bank / available outside bank hours

items.label: (ii)
items.q: Why do we keep our money in a bank?
items.answer: The bank keeps our money safe (1). It helps us save money for our future needs (1). We can also take money out through an ATM or send money to others (1).

answerPoints.point: Helps us save for the future

items.label: (iii)
items.q: How does the post office help people stay connected?
items.answer: It carries letters and parcels from one place to another (1). It sorts letters by region and sends them to the right destination (1). It also sends important documents and money orders (1).

items.label: (iv)
items.q: Modern facilities like flyovers and metros make life easier. What problem did Dada ji point out, and what solution did he suggest?
items.answer: Many animals, birds and trees that used to be there are no longer around because of these changes (1). Development should keep the environment safe by creating a balance (1). If we plant trees, we can keep our environment secure (1).

answerPoints.point: Need a balance between development and environment

items.label: (v)
items.q: What is the barter system? Why was money invented?
items.answer: In the barter system people exchanged goods and services directly, e.g. a farmer exchanged wheat for milk from a shepherd (1). Finding the right trade partner and the right exchange value was not easy (1). Money was invented to make exchanges simple (1).

answerPoints.point: Hard to find partner / right value

blocks.instruction: Complete the table in your answer book.

items.q: Compare communication in earlier times and in present times on these five points: type of communication, speed, frequency (how often), language, and challenges faced.
items.answer: Type: letters, telegram, messengers – now internet, mobile, text messages, video calls (1). Speed: slow, days or weeks – now seconds (1). Frequency: rarely – now many times a day (1). Language: mostly local language, handwritten – now many languages, typed, emojis (1). Challenges: long wait, letters could get lost – now wrong information spreads quickly, needs network and phone (1). 1 mark per row with both columns filled.

items.label: (i)
items.q: The festival on which Navya's Mama sent money to her mother by phone.

items.label: (ii)
items.q: The direction shown at the bottom of a map.

items.label: (iii)
items.q: The vehicles waiting at the school gate along with the school buses.

items.label: (iv)
items.q: A place where a child can keep pocket money savings at home.

items.label: (i)
items.q: It is important to save money.
items.answer: Saved money helps us in our future needs and emergencies (1). It lets us buy something important later or help our family (1).

answerPoints.point: Buy important things later / help family

items.label: (ii)
items.q: We should check whether the news we share on phones is true.
items.answer: Quick messages spread very fast, so wrong information also spreads quickly (1). Sharing false news can confuse or harm people, so we should check with a trusted source or an elder first (1).

answerPoints.point: Can harm people; check with trusted source

items.label: (iii)
items.q: Dada ji sometimes misses writing letters even though mobile phones are faster.
items.answer: He enjoys the joy of writing and receiving a handwritten letter (1). A letter feels personal and is a memory one can keep (1).

answerPoints.point: Personal / can be kept as memory

items.label: (i)
items.q: List the people involved and one vehicle used at a fire station.
items.answer: Firefighters / fire officers (1); fire engine (fire truck) (1).

items.label: (ii)
items.q: Why did so many people come to the hospital that day? What did Dada ji say about the hospital?
items.answer: The hospital was holding an Eye Check-up Camp (1). Dada ji said the hospital is an important part of the community — the doctors there helped his wife see better after her eye operation (1).

answerPoints.point: Important part of community / grandmother's operation

blocks.instruction: Answer in detail (five to six sentences).

items.label: (i)
items.q: Describe how communication has changed from long ago to today. Mention at least four stages.
items.answer: Long ago people used drumbeats and carvings on rocks (1). Later, messengers and pigeons carried letters (1). Then the postal service began, sending letters, parcels and documents (1). Inventions like the telephone, radio and television made sharing information easier (1). Today mobile phones and the internet connect us with anyone, anywhere, in seconds (1).

items.label: (ii)
items.q:
Imagine you have ₹ 100 for a month. Make a simple budget: how much will you save and how much will you spend, on what, and why? How will saving help you in future?
OR
Write five public places in your neighbourhood and one service each of them provides.
items.answer: Budget option: a savings amount and a spending amount that add up to ₹ 100 (1); at least two spending items like stationery, snacks (1); a reason for the amounts chosen (1); how saving helps in future, e.g. buying something big, emergencies (1); neat, complete sentences (1). OR option: 1 mark for each public place with a correct service (hospital – treatment; post office – letters; police station – safety; library – books; bus stop – travel; bank – keeps money safe).
items.markingGuide: Complete and sensible on either option — 5; mostly complete — 3; only one or two relevant points — 1.

items.q: Draw a simple map of the route from your home to your school. Mark the four directions (N, S, E, W) and show at least two landmarks such as a park, shop, temple or bus stop.
items.answer: Map shows home and school joined by a route (1); N at the top with S, E, W correctly placed (1); at least two landmarks drawn and named (1).
items.markingGuide: Route + correct directions + two landmarks — 3; two of these — 2; one — 1.

items.q: During COVID-19, many people in the neighbourhood helped the community. Name two such people, write how they helped, and why it is important to thank them.
items.answer: Two helpers, e.g. doctors, nurses, garbage collectors, shopkeepers, police, teachers (1); how they helped — treated the sick, kept the area clean, supplied food, taught online (1); thanking them shows respect for their courage and hard work and encourages everyone to help each other (1).
